q: In the FortiOS CLI, what do the top-level command categories config, get, show, and execute do, and how does an operator get context-sensitive help?
kp: config enters read-write configuration tree
get displays read-only system info
show displays current configuration objects
execute runs one-off operations (ping, test, reset, api)
press ? at any prompt for context-sensitive help

q: How does command abbreviation work in the FortiOS CLI, and how do you see the full form of an abbreviated command?
kp: commands/parameters may be abbreviated to the shortest unique prefix
the shortest unique prefix of a command or parameter is accepted (e.g. conf sys int = config system interface)
? shows full spelling of recognized commands/params

q: What do the CLI keywords next, end, clear and the exit command do in the configuration tree?
kp: next: saves the current table entry and returns to the entries prompt (so you can add the next entry)
end: saves and exits the subcommand entirely, returning to the parent prompt
clear: clears/resets a parameter
exit: moves up one level without saving (aborts the current level)

q: How are strings containing special characters or spaces entered in the FortiOS CLI?
kp: quote the string in single or double quotes, or prefix the special character with a backslash (AG p.79)
special characters that cannot be used directly: < > ( ) # ' " (and spaces); ? and Tab need Ctrl+V first in the CLI console

q: In FortiOS CLI, when you 'set' a multi-value parameter (like allowaccess), does it replace the previous values or add to them? How do you explicitly add or remove individual values?
kp: append: adds a value to a list without replacing existing values
unselect: removes a value from a list

q: What do the CLI commands select, unselect and append do?
kp: select: sets/selects a value
unselect: removes a value from a list
append: adds to a list or config table without replacing existing items

q: Show how to assign IP address 10.0.0.1/24 to interface port1 and enable ping, SSH and HTTPS management access on it.
kp: config system interface
edit port1
set allowaccess ping ssh https (list)

q: What does the allowaccess interface parameter control, and what is the default allowaccess on regular physical interfaces vs the dedicated management port?
kp: allowaccess controls which management protocols (ping/https/ssh/gateway, etc.) are allowed on each interface
AG example: LAN port1 with set allowaccess ping https ssh
AG example: WAN port2 with set allowaccess ping

q: How do you create a link aggregation (aggregate) interface from two physical ports and give it an IP?
kp: create the interface under config system interface with set type aggregate
create aggregate member list
set ip on the aggregate interface

q: How do you create a VLAN interface (VLAN 100 on port1) with IP 192.168.100.1/24?
kp: config system interface
edit vlan100 or vlan object with vlanid 100
set interface port1 (parent)
set vlanid 100

q: What does 'set dedicated-to management' do on a system interface and how does it relate to the HA reserved management interface?
kp: marks an interface as the dedicated management interface
mgmt traffic uses it instead of data interfaces
in HA, reserved mgmt interface config (incl. ha-mgmt-interface-gateway) is not synchronized

q: Show a complete firewall policy in CLI: allow traffic from LAN (port2, address 'lan-subnet') to WAN (port1) using service 'ALL', with NAT enabled, schedule 'All'.
kp: config firewall policy
edit 1
set srcintf port2
set dstintf port1
set srcaddr lan-subnet
set dstaddr all
set schedule All
set service ALL
set action accept
set nat enable

q: How is NAT enabled on a firewall policy, and how do you use an IP pool for outbound NAT instead of the outgoing interface address?
kp: NAT is enabled per policy with set nat enable (manual, not automatic)
By default the outgoing interface address is used for NAT
set ippool <pool> references a pool created in config firewall ippool

q: How does firewall policy ordering work in FortiOS? What happens when no policy matches, and how do you move a policy?
kp: policies are evaluated top-down, first match wins
no match -> implicit deny (final implicit deny policy)
use CLI move (e.g. 'move <id> before <id>') or GUI reorder; policy ID order = evaluation order

q: What is the difference between an explicit deny policy and the implicit deny in FortiOS firewall policy evaluation?
kp: explicit deny = a policy with action deny you create (logged, can be placed anywhere)
implicit deny = the built-in final policy that denies everything not matched (always present, ID last)

q: Show how to create a firewall service object named 'my-svc' for TCP port 8443 and reference it in a policy.
kp: config firewall service custom
edit my-svc
set tcp-portrange 8443
end
reference with 'set service my-svc' in the policy

q: How do you define a firewall address object with a mix of an IP range and a single host, and use it as source in a policy?
kp: one address object holds one type only — the IP range is its own object (set type iprange + set start-ip <a> + set end-ip <b>) and the single host its own object (set subnet <ip> 255.255.255.255)
the mixed source is combined in an address group (config firewall addrgrp, set member <obj1> <obj2>)
policy references the group: set srcaddr <group>

q: Show a static route in CLI to send 10.10.0.0/24 via gateway 10.0.0.254 on interface port1, with distance 10.
kp: set device port1
set gateway 10.0.0.254
set distance 10

q: How is the default gateway set on a FortiGate, and what is the difference between 'set defaultgw enable' on an interface and a static 0.0.0.0/0 route?
kp: defaultgw enable on interface makes that interface the default GW (adds implicit 0/0 via that interface's gateway)
explicit: config router static 0.0.0.0/0 with device+gateway
interface defaultgw requires gateway reachable on that subnet

q: Show a minimal BGP configuration: AS 65001, neighbor 10.0.0.254 in AS 65002, advertising no network by default.
kp: config router bgp
set as 65001
config neighbor
set remote-as 65002

q: What CLI commands show the routing table (all protocols, and only static routes)?
kp: get router info routing-table all
get router info routing-table static

q: Show a complete site-to-site IPsec tunnel in CLI: phase1 'peer1' with static remote gateway 203.0.113.1, PSK 'secret', IKEv2, phase2 'tun1' for 10.1.0.0/24 <-> 10.2.0.0/24 ESP 3DES SHA1. Use exact 7.6.7 parameter names.
kp: config vpn ipsec phase1-interface (interface-based phase1 object in 7.6.7)
set remote-gw 203.0.113.1 (static gateway)
set ike-version 2
set psksecret secret
config vpn ipsec phase2-interface
set src-subnet for 10.1.0.0/24 (accept CIDR 10.1.0.0/24 or ip+mask 10.1.0.0 255.255.255.0)
set dst-subnet for 10.2.0.0/24 (accept CIDR 10.2.0.0/24 or ip+mask 10.2.0.0 255.255.255.0)
ESP 3DES + SHA1: set encryption 3des and set hash sha1

q: In 7.6.7 config vpn ipsec phase1-interface, what is the difference between a static remote gateway and a dynamic one (e.g., ADVPN)?
kp: Static: set remote-gw is the known, fixed gateway IP address
Dynamic (ADVPN): the gateway address is learned through the tunnel — ADVPN is the documented dynamic mode in the 7.6.7 AG

q: In 7.6.7 phase2-interface, what are the src-addr-type values (subnet / range / name) and when do you use each?
kp: subnet: one IPv4 subnet per side (src-subnet/dst-subnet)
range: an IP range per side (src-end-ip/dst-end-ip)
name: reference a firewall address or address group object

q: FortiOS supports IPsec over TCP. Explain when this is used, which port, and minimum firmware/client versions.
kp: used when UDP/500 and UDP/4500 are blocked (CGNAT, ISPs)
TCP transport, default port 443
supported on FortiOS 7.4.2+; FortiClient 7.4.1+; IKE over TCP with ESP encapsulated in TCP

q: How do you configure Dead Peer Detection (DPD) on an IPsec phase1, and what do the mode and interval values control?
kp: set dpd [disable|on-idle|on-demand|...] (field is dpd in 7.6.7, not dpd-mode)
set dpd-retrycount <n>
set dpd-retryinterval <seconds>
DPD sends probe messages (every 5 seconds by default) to detect a dead peer

q: How is NPU (ASIC) offload of IPsec traffic controlled in 7.6, and how do you verify it is working?
kp: config vpn ipsec phase1/phase1-interface: set npu-offload enable/disable (default enable)
verify: diagnose vpn tunnel list — npu_flag 03 = bidirectional NPU processing, counters rxp/txp tick

q: What happened to SSL VPN tunnel mode in FortiOS 7.6, and what must an administrator do before upgrading to 7.6.3+?
kp: proprietary SSL VPN tunnel mode replaced by standards-based IPsec VPN in 7.6.3+
existing tunnel-mode configs (and related firewall policies) are NOT upgraded — removed on upgrade
must manually migrate to IPsec VPN (GUI/CLI/FortiConverter) before upgrading to 7.6.3

q: What is 'Agentless VPN' in FortiOS 7.6, and what was it previously called?
kp: Agentless VPN = the former SSL VPN web mode (browser-based, no agent)
config persists across the 7.6 upgrade under the new name

q: Which FortiClient version is required to use IPsec VPN over TCP transport, and since which FortiOS version is IPsec-over-TCP supported?
kp: FortiClient 7.4.1 or later
FortiOS 7.4.2 or later

q: Show a basic FGCP active-passive HA cluster configuration in CLI: group 1, priority 100, heartbeat on port10, monitor interface port1, virtual IP 10.0.0.99/24.
kp: set mode a-p (active-passive)
set group-id 1 (field name is group-id in 7.6.7, not "set group")
set priority 100
set hbdev port10 1 (heartbeat interface with weight)
set monitor port1 1 (monitored interface)

q: Which settings are NOT synchronized between FortiGate HA cluster members?
kp: host name
HA override / device priority
virtual cluster priority
GUI dashboard widgets
HA reserved management interface settings (incl. ha-mgmt-interface-gateway)
most subscriptions/licenses (each unit licensed individually; FortiToken Mobile is an exception)

q: What is FGSP and in what topology is it used instead of an FGCP cluster?
kp: FortiGate Session Life Support Protocol
synchronizes sessions and configuration across standalone FortiGates or HA clusters, allowing horizontal scaling of sessions across locations
configured via config system standalone-cluster (FGSP attributes) with config cluster-peer (set peerip) and config session-sync-filter to select which sessions synchronize

q: What criteria determine which unit becomes the primary (active) unit in an FGCP cluster?
kp: Override disabled (default): the unit with the most HA uptime becomes primary (MUPS order: uptime, session count, firmware version, serial)
HA uptime difference less than 300 seconds counts as a tie; monitored-interface failure or member restart resets HA uptime to zero
Override enabled: priority value takes precedence over uptime (MPUS order)
Standardize override across all members — mixed enable/disable causes unpredictable elections

q: What triggers an automatic failover in an FGCP HA cluster?
kp: primary unit failure (device down or a directly monitored link down) triggers failover
link monitor (config system link-monitor) failure adds its ha-priority penalty to the unit's Global Penalty; with multiple servers the monitor is failed only if ALL servers stop responding
failover triggers only when the Global Penalty reaches or exceeds pingserver-failover-threshold (0-50, default 0 = immediate failover on first monitor failure)

q: How do you authenticate to the FortiOS REST API v2, and what are the requirements for the token and transport?
kp: API token (generated by admin or via api-user), sent as Authorization: Bearer <token> header
HTTPS required (self-signed cert by default)
token expiry configurable 1-10080 minutes (config system settings set restapi-token-ttl)

q: What does the 7.6.7 AG document about REST API v2 URLs, and where is the complete API reference?
kp: URL pattern https://<host>/api/v2/...
/api/v2/monitor/<schema> endpoints for monitoring data (e.g., SD-WAN interface-log, sla-log, health-check)
Some endpoints are retired (e.g., monitor/system/security-rating/*)
Complete REST API reference is in Fortinet KYC Network (FKYC)

q: Show the CLI steps to create a REST API administrator and generate its API token.
kp: config system api-user / edit <name>
set api-key <key> (the 7.6.7 CLI field — not "set password")
set accprofile <profile> (least privilege)
config trusthost with set ipv4-trusthost <subnet> (0.0.0.0/0 not permitted)
execute api-user generate-key <name> [expiry in minutes]

q: What must be configured for browser-based (JavaScript) calls to the FortiOS REST API, and why?
kp: CORS Allow Origin must be configured on the API user (config system api-user > set cors-allow-origin) because the browser Same-Origin Policy blocks cross-origin JavaScript calls until the server sends Access-Control-Allow-Origin
the request must carry Bearer token auth (Authorization: Bearer <key>); wildcard origins should be avoided where possible

q: Where does the complete FortiOS REST API v2 object catalog live, and what is publicly available without a subscription?
kp: full catalog (all API objects/parameters) is in Fortinet FKYC (FortiKnowledge) — subscription (FortiCare) only
public docs: API chapters in the Administration Guide cover general usage, token auth, examples

q: Where is the complete REST API v2 reference documented, and what does the 7.6.7 AG document about creating REST API administrators?
kp: Complete REST API reference is in Fortinet KYC Network (FKYC)
Only the super_admin profile can create REST API administrators
GUI fields include Administrator Profile, PKI Group, CORS Allow Origin, and Trusted Hosts
CLI: config system api-user with set api-key, set accprofile, config trusthost
Token is displayed only once; expiry set via generate-key [minutes]

q: What 7.6.7 change in default behavior affects factory-reset / out-of-box initialization on FortiGate 20xG models?
kp: Bug 1288059: on 20xG models, port1 and port2 are removed from the virtual switch after factory reset or out-of-box initialization
These ports are configured for DHCP by default to support Zero Touch Provisioning (ZTP)

q: What changed in FortiOS 7.6 regarding the CLI prompt and 'show system status' for HA members?
kp: The CLI prompt now includes the device HA role (Primary/Secondary) — issue 1256231
The role label updates automatically after a failover
The prompt format change may break automation that relies on fixed prompt patterns (e.g., Ansible)
extra: verify exact change from release notes CLI changes chapter

q: What changed in 7.6.7 regarding the default MTU of IPsec tunnel interfaces?
kp: Bug 1248524: in 8.0.0 the default IPsec tunnel MTU changed from 1420 to 1402 on a listed set of models
In 8.0.1/7.6.7 the 1420-to-1402 change was extended to all FortiGate models
extra: exact version + values from release notes

q: What new FortiASIC/NPU option did 7.6.7 introduce for VLAN accounting on NP7 devices?
kp: 1192303: config system npu / set vlan-accounting {disable|enable}; enabled by default
set vlan-acct-interval <milliseconds> — default 200, range 100 to 10000

q: Which FortiGate models are supported in FortiOS 7.6.7?
kp: FortiOS 7.6.7 (build 3704) supported-model list is in the 7.6.7 Release Notes, 'Introduction and supported models' (p.8)
FortiGate line: FG-30G through FG-7000F (~60 models), incl. 200E/201E/300E/400E/500E/600E/1100E/1101E/2000E/2200E/3300E/3600E/3960E/3980E/5001E and hyperscale FG-6000F/7000E/7000F
also FortiWiFi (FWF-*), FortiGate Rugged (FGR-*), FortiFirewall appliances (FFW-*) with FFW-VM64/FFW-VM64-KVM, and VM images FG-VM64* (x86) and FG-ARM64-* (AWS/Azure/GCP/KVM/OCI)
no '100E/1000E/3000E/4000E' series in the 7.6.7 list

q: If upgrading from FortiOS 7.4.4 to 7.6.7, what VPN-related migration must happen and what FortiManager version is required for managed devices?
kp: SSL VPN tunnel mode must be migrated to IPsec VPN before the upgrade (removed in 7.6.3+)
FortiManager must be upgraded to 7.6.3 before upgrading FortiOS to 7.6.3+, re-import config

q: Show how to list all IPsec tunnels and interpret key fields of 'diagnose vpn tunnel list' output.
kp: diagnose vpn tunnel list
fields: name, ver (IKEv1/2), serial, local->remote, tun_id, bound_if, lgwy, proxyid_num, child_num, refcnt, ilast/olast, ad, stat rxp/txp/rxb/txb, npu flag, dpd mode

q: Show the exact CLI commands to enable and run a real-time IKE debug with a filter for a specific remote IP.
kp: diagnose vpn ike log filter rem-addr4 <ip>
diagnose debug application ike -1
diagnose debug enable
(stop: diagnose debug disable)

q: How do you list active firewall sessions in the CLI, and what information does the output include?
kp: diagnose sys session list
output shows session status, flags, timeouts, src/dst ip:port, protocol, serial number

q: How do you capture packets on a FortiGate interface in the CLI (tcpdump) and what are the stop commands?
kp: diagnose sniffer packet <interface> <filter>
Stop the capture with Ctrl+C

q: How can an operator search the FortiNet Community support forums for FortiOS 7.6.7 issues without a UI (server-side), and where are topic pages located?
kp: GET https://community.fortinet.com/search/?query=<terms>
topic URLs: https://community.fortinet.com/<category>/<topic-slug>-<id>
sitemaps: community.fortinet.com/sitemap-topics-1.xml / -2.xml (~100k topics)

q: From a server (datacenter IP), how do you fetch recent r/FortiNet posts, and what endpoints are blocked?
kp: RSS works: https://www.reddit.com/r/FortiNet/.rss (or old.reddit.com/.rss)
JSON API (hot.json/search.json) and HTML are 403 from datacenter IPs
use web search as historical backfill

q: How do you look up a known FortiOS bug by ID (e.g. 1306049), and what are the official channels for bug info?
kp: Fortinet PSIRT / FortiGuard Security Research bulletins
release notes 'Known issues' chapter lists bug IDs
FortiCare (subscription) has full bug database (FKYC)
community.fortinet.com threads discuss field impact

q: On FortiOS 7.6.7, how do you enable SD-WAN, where are SD-WAN rules configured, and what load-balance modes are available?
kp: enable under config system sdwan with set status enable
SD-WAN rules are configured as config service under config system sdwan (the CLI Reference describes them as 'SD-WAN rules (also called services)')
load-balance-mode options include source-ip-based, weight-based, usage-based, source-dest-ip-based, and measured-volume-based

q: You want an SD-WAN service to prefer members meeting an SLA but keep traffic on the current member unless the SLA fails. Which fields implement this and how?
kp: set priority-members lists the preferred member sequence numbers
set minimum-sla-meet-members requires at least N members to pass the SLA
set sla-stickiness enable keeps traffic sticky to the current member
set tie-break (zone, cfg-order, etc.) resolves ties between members
set hold-down-time delays failover/failback flapping

q: Write the outline of an active SD-WAN health check that pings a server every 10 seconds, weighs latency and packet loss, and defines an SLA with latency and packet-loss thresholds.
kp: config health-check under config system sdwan with set detect-mode active
set server specifies the remote server address
set interval 10000 for the probe interval (interval is in milliseconds, so 10 s = 10000)
set probe-count and probe-timeout control probes
set failtime and recoverytime control member state transitions
set latency-weight and set packet-loss-weight score the measurement
nested config sla with set latency-threshold and set packetloss-threshold defines the SLA

q: How can an SD-WAN service match traffic by FortiGuard internet service instead of by application ID?
kp: set internet-service enable activates internet-service matching
set internet-service-fortiguard matches FortiGuard internet services
set internet-service-name matches named internet services
set internet-service-app-ctrl / internet-service-app-ctrl-category / internet-service-group extend matching
set internet-service-custom allows custom internet service entries

q: What are SD-WAN zones in FortiOS 7.6.7 and which settings do they expose?
kp: config zone under config system sdwan defines SD-WAN zones
set minimum-sla-meet-members per zone
set service-sla-tie-break with cfg-order, fib-best-match, and other options
set advpn-select enables Advanced VPN participation in the zone
services reference zones via priority-zone / zone-mode

q: Which CLI objects make up the FortiGate ZTNA access proxy in FortiOS 7.6.8, and what role does each play?
kp: config ztna web-proxy configures the ZTNA access proxy (web proxy)
config ztna web-portal configures the ZTNA web portal (auth-portal, bookmarks, FortiClient download)
config ztna reverse-connector configures the reverse connector
config ztna traffic-forward-proxy configures traffic forwarding
the ZTNA access proxy can act as an inline CASB for SaaS traffic using ZTNA access control rules

q: Describe the API gateway and real-server configuration under a ZTNA web-proxy in the FortiOS CLI.
kp: config api-gateway under config ztna web-proxy with set ldb-method (static, round-robin, etc.)
set persistence [none|http-cookie] controls client affinity
QUIC settings are nested under config quic
config realservers with set address/set ip, set port, set status [active|standby]
real-server health check via set health-check and set health-check-proto
set weight for load balancing, set verify-cert for backend certificate validation

q: List the DLP configuration object types in the FortiOS 7.6.7 CLI Reference and what each defines.
kp: config dlp data-type defines predefined/custom data types
config dlp dictionary defines dictionaries
config dlp exact-data-match defines exact data match entries
config dlp filepattern defines file pattern matching
config dlp profile defines DLP profiles with rules
config dlp sensor groups dictionaries/rules
config dlp settings holds global DLP settings

q: Show the DLP profile configuration pattern for a proxy feature set that blocks traffic matching a sensor, including the protocols a rule can cover.
kp: config dlp profile with set feature-set proxy
config rule with set proto covering smtp, pop3, imap, http-get, http-post, ftp, nntp, mapi, ssh, cifs, websocket
set filter-by sensor selects sensor-based filtering
set sensor <name> references the DLP sensor
set action block blocks matching traffic
websocket DLP requires enabling the websocket profile protocol under config firewall profile-protocol-options

q: How is inline CASB configured on a FortiGate firewall policy in 7.6.7? Give the CLI pattern for the CASB profile and the policy.
kp: config casb profile with nested config saas-application
nested config access-rule under the SaaS application with set action (e.g. block)
policy side: set casb-profile <profile> on the firewall policy
policy must set inspection-mode proxy
policy must reference an ssl-ssh-profile using deep inspection
policy must set utm-status enable

q: Which CLI objects support explicit web proxy configuration in FortiOS 7.6.8?
kp: config web-proxy explicit configures explicit proxy settings
config web-proxy global holds global proxy settings
config web-proxy profile defines proxy profiles
config web-proxy url-match defines URL matching
config web-proxy forward-server / forward-server-group for upstream forwarding
config web-proxy isolator-server / wisp / fast-fallback / debug-url are additional proxy objects

q: How do you configure an access proxy VIP and a virtual host for explicit proxy in the FortiOS CLI?
kp: config firewall vip with set type access-proxy
set server-type [https|ssh] and set extip/extintf/extport
set empty-cert-action [accept|block|accept-unmanageable]
set user-agent-detect and set client-cert options
config firewall access-proxy-virtual-host with set host and set host-type [sub-string|wildcard]

q: Which CLI objects manage the NPU on FortiGate models with network processors in 7.6.7?
kp: config system npu (CLI Reference p.1786) manages NPU offload
config system npu-post manages post-NPU processing
config system npu-setting prp manages parallel path processing settings
config system npu-vlink manages NPU virtual links

q: Which settings are available for NP7 HPE processors under config system npu (the NPU attributes object), and what do they control?
kp: dedicated-management-cpu {disable|enable}
npu-group-effective-scope {0|1|2|3|255}
hash-config {src-dst-ip|5-tuple|src-ip} selects flow hashing
capwap-offload {disable|enable} offloads CAPWAP traffic to the NPU
napi-break-interval controls NAPI polling

q: In what order does the FortiOS 7.6 parallel path processing pipeline handle a packet?
kp: Ingress first, then Admission control
Kernel, then Destination NAT
Routing (including SD-WAN), then Stateful inspection
Policy lookup, then Session management
Session helpers, User authentication, Device identification follow
Agentless VPN and local management stages complete the pipeline

q: How is multi-VDOM mode enabled on FortiOS 7.6.7 and how do interfaces get assigned to VDOMs?
kp: config system global with set vdom-mode multi-vdom
interfaces are assigned with set vdom <vdom> under config system interface
on models with NPU virtual links, switching to multi-vdom automatically creates npu0_vlink0 and npu0_vlink1 in the root VDOM
two directly connected vlink interfaces in the same VDOM plus an all-to-all multicast policy creates a multicast loop

q: How do you configure DNS servers for non-management VDOMs in FortiOS 7.6.7?
kp: config system vdom-dns is the global object that configures DNS servers for non-management VDOMs
set vdom-dns enable turns on VDOM-specific DNS
set primary and set secondary for IPv4 DNS servers
set ip6-primary / set ip6-secondary for IPv6
set protocol [cleartext|dot|doh] selects DNS transport
set interface-select-method [auto|sdwan|specify] chooses the outbound interface

q: Which CLI object family configures the FortiGate wireless LAN controller in 7.6.7?
kp: config wireless-controller vap and vap-group for SSIDs
config wireless-controller wtp, wtp-profile, wtp-group for FortiAP management
config wireless-controller apcfg-profile, mpsk-profile, wids-profile, qos-profile, nac-profile, ssid-policy for controller policies
config wireless-controller setting and timers hold controller settings
diagnose sys wireless iwconfig is used for wireless diagnostics

q: What is a WTP profile in the FortiGate wireless controller and name four settings it exposes?
kp: WTP profile (FortiAP profile) defines radio settings for manageable FortiAP platforms
set ap-country selects the regulatory country
set ap-handoff controls AP-to-AP handoff
set admin-auth-tacacs+ allows TACACS+ for AP administration
apcfg-auto-cert settings (protocol none/est/..., CA/HTTP/SCEP enrollment fields) manage AP auto-certificates

q: How do you set up FSSO on a FortiGate with a Windows AD FSSO agent collector, and what does the connector do?
kp: config user fsso configures FSSO NTLM authentication
FSSO agent connector is created under Security Fabric > External Connectors (FSSO Agent on Windows AD)
set the primary FSSO agent IP and password
set ldap-server <AD-LDAP-server> to point at the AD LDAP server
enable proactive group retrieval with set ldap-poll enable (set ldap-poll-filter, set ldap-poll-interval)
the FSSO agent sends AD logon events (username + IP address) to the FortiGate, which stores them and builds FSSO user groups

q: How are hardware FortiTokens registered on a FortiGate, and what 2FA-related components does the Administration Guide cover?
kp: config user fortitoken with edit <serial_number> imports hard tokens
GUI: User & Authentication > FortiTokens > Import for bulk import
the AG covers FortiToken Mobile push (FTM) and FortiIdentity Cloud
the AG covers two-factor authentication scenarios including IPsec IKEv2 2FA with EAP and certificate authentication
two-factor filter is used when synchronizing AD users to FortiIdentity Cloud

q: How does FortiOS 7.6.7 protect access to generative AI applications using web filtering and application control, and what log fields does GenAI monitoring produce?
kp: web filter protection uses the FortiGuard Artificial Intelligence Technology category, which is category 100 in the CLI
application-control protection uses the FortiGuard GenAI application category with deep packet inspection enabled
GenAI monitoring log fields include aiuser, model, dcgeo, usecase, prompt, and cloudgenai
FortiView AI Applications and AI Use Cases dashboard widgets monitor AI traffic in real time

q: How are FortiOS 7.6.7 log message IDs organized, and give two concrete examples with their numeric IDs.
kp: the Log Reference groups messages by category with numeric LOGID ranges
attack anomaly logs: 18432 LOGID_ATTCK_ANOMALY_TCP_UDP, 18433 LOGID_ATTCK_ANOMALY_ICMP, 18434 LOGID_ATTCK_ANOMALY_OTHERS
application control logs start at 28672 (LOGID_APP_CTRL_IM_BASIC)
each LOGID entry documents the message text and its fields

q: What extended log examples does the 7.6.7 Log Reference include, and why are extended logs useful?
kp: extended log example for explicit proxy logging
extended log example for DLP inspection
extended logs add detailed fields beyond the standard event log
the reference documents fields for each log type

q: Which CLI objects configure SNMP on a FortiGate in 7.6.7?
kp: config system snmp community for SNMP community strings
config system snmp mib-view for MIB views
config system snmp user for SNMP users (v3)
config system snmp sysinfo and config system snmp rmon-stat for system information objects
the FortiGate MIB information overview explains using MIB files for SNMP operations

q: What does the FortiGate 6000F administration guide cover for hardware operations, and how do you verify component health?
kp: the guide covers the FortiGate 6000F chassis with management boards
MGMT1 and MGMT2 management board connections for GUI/CLI access
back panel PSU and fan try LEDs should be solid green during normal operation
front panel LEDs indicate alarm, HA, and power state
interface LEDs indicate connected network interfaces

q: What module-based architecture does the FortiGate 7000F use, and what does its administration guide document?
kp: the 7000F uses FPM (fixed port module) and FIM (flexible interface module) chassis modules
FIM-7941F and FIM-7921F interface modules with configurable interface assignments (e.g. FIM-7941F ports 1-18, M1, M2)
FIM-7941F includes NP7 processors
the guide documents replacing failed FPM or FIM modules in standalone and HA cluster configurations
it documents formatting FIM/FPM boot devices and installing firmware on them

q: Summarize the firmware upgrade guide's pre-upgrade checklist and the upgrade methods it documents.
kp: pre-upgrade checklist: verify support contract status (FMWR license and FortiCare support contract)
confirm target version and maturity: Feature vs Mature release
validate that the device model is supported in the target release
determine the supported upgrade path using the Fortinet Upgrade Path Tool; skipping intermediate versions may cause configuration issues
review the full release notes, including behavior changes, CLI changes, and known issues
upgrade methods: standalone upgrade, HA (FGCP) cluster upgrade, FGSP upgrade, and FortiManager managed devices upgrade
Fabric Upgrade updates all FortiGates, FortiAPs, and FortiSwitches to the root FortiGate's target version via System > Fabric Management

q: How is carrier-grade NAT pool allocation configured on FortiOS, and what does the CGN architecture guide document about port block allocation, SPA, and monitoring?
kp: the CGN pool is a firewall IP pool: config firewall ippool with set type port-block-allocation (cgn-resource-allocation)
pool fields include startip, endip, cgn-block-size (64 to 4096, minimum 64 ports), cgn-port-start and cgn-port-end
cgn-spa enables sticky port allocation so one public IP sticks to the client across concurrent sessions (port block size 1)
utilization-alarm-raise and utilization-alarm-clear configure SNMP utilization alarms
NAT64 translation between IPv6 clients and IPv4 hosts is supported in the pool (set nat64)
diagnose firewall ippool list user shows per-user PBA allocation; config monitoring npu-hpe and diagnose npu np7 hpe monitor HPE activity

q: What deployment blueprints does the SD-WAN 7.6 Architecture for MSSPs document, and what overlay/monitoring capabilities does it cover?
kp: the document covers the Fortinet Secure SD-WAN/SD-Branch reference architecture written primarily for managed service providers
deployment blueprints include Spokes as Edge CPEs, Hubs, and three hub blueprints: MSSP premises multitenant, MSSP premises no multitenancy, and customer premises
public cloud management blueprints include multitenant with direct customer access and multitenant with FortiPortal
overlay network designs cover routing designs, overlay topologies interconnecting SD-WAN sites, and multi-VRF segmentation
monitoring chapters cover FortiMonitor, FortiAIOps, and external orchestration; central management uses FortiManager and FortiAnalyzer

q: After upgrading FortiGate 1800F/1801F to FortiOS 7.6.8, which SFP ports are affected by the traffic-forwarding bug and what are the remediation options per the community knowledge base?
kp: an internal driver update in 7.6.8 makes GE SFP ports 17-20 unable to process traffic on 1800F/1801F
traffic on GE SFP ports 21-24 and 25-40 and GE RJ45 ports is unaffected
the issue is tracked as bug ID 1353422
a special build (8768) has been released; contacting Fortinet support is required to obtain it
staying on GA build 3744, the workaround is moving connections to ports 21-24

q: Why does administrator SSO authentication fail after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8, which login methods are affected, and how is the issue confirmed and worked around?
kp: administrator SSO fails with 'Single Sign-On Failed' with no option to enter SSO credentials
affected: administrator FortiCloud SSO, third-party SSO (e.g. SAML/Entra ID), and Security Fabric SSO with root FortiGate as IdP
not affected: VPN user SSO, local admin authentication, and RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ admin authentication
confirmed by a 'FORTISM Violation' in the crashlog (diagnose debug crashlog read | grep <date>)
only FortiOS 7.6.8 is affected (7.2.14, 7.4.13, 7.6.7, 8.0.2 are not)
fix is scheduled for FortiOS 7.6.9; the workaround is using a local or RADIUS/LDAP/TACACS+ admin account

q: What causes FortiGate to enter memory conserve mode after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8, how is it diagnosed, and what resolves it?
kp: the default IPSEngine 7.01200 shipped with FortiOS 7.6.8 causes conserve mode on devices using an IPS profile
diagnosed with diagnose sys top-mem (ipsengine processes consuming several GB) and diagnose debug crashlog read | grep 'conserve mode'
get system performance status (abbreviated: get sys perf status) shows high memory usage
resolved by IPSEngine 7.01204, obtained by logging a support ticket

q: What changed in Central SNAT policies after upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.1 and how can the pre-upgrade per-SD-WAN-member behavior be emulated?
kp: from 7.6.1, Central SNAT policies no longer support individual SD-WAN members as selectable interfaces; only SD-WAN zones and non-SD-WAN interfaces may be selected
SD-WAN members are removed from existing Central SNAT policies during the upgrade
pre-upgrade behavior can be emulated by setting associated-interface on the IP pool (config firewall ippool) to the SD-WAN member, then adding that pool to the central-snat-map
in 7.6.1/7.6.2 a GUI bug hid SD-WAN zones on the Central SNAT menu (issue ID 1107003), resolved in 7.6.3; the CLI workaround should not be edited via GUI afterwards

q: Why do FortiGate 30/31G devices fail upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8 with a firmware signature verification error, and how is it resolved? What does the 'inflate() error: -3' console message mean?
kp: the 'This Firmware didn't pass the signature verification' error is a known issue specific to the 30/31G platform when upgrading from 7.6.7 to 7.6.8
resolution: first upgrade to the FortiOS 7.6.7 STS special build 8767 (obtained via a TAC ticket), then upgrade to 7.6.8 GA: 7.6.7 GA -> 8767 -> 7.6.8 GA
alternatively the device can be upgraded via FortiManager
'inflate() error: -3' during upgrade means the device lacks free RAM to proceed; workaround is setting the IPS engine-count to 1 (config ips global) and rebooting before retrying

q: What are the most important special notices and behavior changes an administrator must handle when upgrading to FortiOS 7.6.8 (and since 7.6.3)?
kp: since FortiOS 7.6.3, SSL VPN tunnel mode is replaced by IPsec VPN (can use TCP port 443); SSL VPN tunnel mode is gone from GUI and CLI and its settings are NOT upgraded from previous versions
customers must migrate SSL VPN tunnel mode configuration to IPsec VPN before upgrading to 7.6.3+
Agentless VPN (formerly SSL VPN web mode) is unavailable on 2GB-RAM models such as 40F, 50G, 60F, 61F, FGR-60F (2GB), 70G, 90G, 91G; settings are not upgraded
RAM can be checked with diagnose hardware sysinfo conserve (total RAM below 2000 MB = 2 GB model)
migrating affected models to IPsec Dialup VPN is recommended for remote access

q: What are the key 8.0.0 release facts for the FortiOS 8.0 line, including what changed for FortiGate WiFi Controller and notable CLI additions?
kp: FortiOS 8.0.0 is the GA release of the 8.0 line; 8.0.2 is the latest patch release in the line
FortiGate WiFi Controller on 8.0.0 no longer supports FortiAP-C, FortiAP-U E-series, and FortiAP-W2 E-series except FAP-221E, 223E, 421E and 423E
8.0.0 adds NP7 session accounting interval range 1-600 seconds (set session-acct-interval) and sw-np-rate/sw-np-rate-unit/sw-np-rate-burst for NP7-to-ISF bandwidth control
8.0.0 adds IPv6 address pool support in explicit proxy policies (set poolname6 under config firewall proxy-policy) and ses-denied-multicast-traffic under config system settings

q: Which FortiOS release lines and latest versions should a specialist know about as of late 2026, and what does the firmware upgrade guide require before performing an upgrade?
kp: the 7.6.x line is at 7.6.8 GA (latest); the 8.x line is the 8.0 line only - FortiOS 8.2 and 8.4 do not exist
8.0.0 GA plus 8.0.2 is the latest 8.0.x patch

pre-upgrade: verify support contract status (FMWR license + FortiCare), confirm target version maturity (Feature vs Mature), validate device model support, determine the supported upgrade path with the Fortinet Upgrade Path Tool (skipping intermediate versions may cause configuration issues), and read the full release notes
upgrade methods include standalone, FGCP cluster, FGSP, and FortiManager-managed device upgrades
